conventions.convention: Logarithms are natural; entropy and encoder rates are measured in nats per source symbol. Zero entropy terms use 0 ln 0 = 0.
The source vectors are IID across times t ≥ 1; terminals within a vector may be dependent. There are k ≥ 2 finite nonempty source alphabets. The empty complement is a singleton product.

Codes have separate deterministic encoders and one common deterministic decoder. Achievability allows increasing blocklength subsequences, vanishing block-error probability, and coordinate rate limsups bounded by the target rates.
Joint typicality excludes zero-probability joint letters and imposes empirical-coordinate, full-information, and every nonempty-subset conditional-information bounds.

The deterministic common part is the support-graph component label, with arbitrary fixed labels on zero-marginal symbols. Wyner common information is a separate infimum over finite auxiliaries making X and Y conditionally independent.
The random-binning ensemble assigns labels independently both across distinct words and across encoders.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite-alphabet IID k-source with k ≥ 2, achievable fixed-length lossless rate vectors are exactly the nonnegative vectors satisfying sum_{i∈S} R_i ≥ H_P(X_S | X_{Sᶜ}) for every nonempty S ⊆ [k].

For each fixed nonempty S and every η > 0, there is δ > 0 such that, for every n ≥ 1, fixed complement block, and ε > 0, the number of compatible jointly typical S-blocks is at most (n+1)^|X| exp(n(H_P(X_S | X_{Sᶜ})+η)).
For every δ, ε > 0, a finite-alphabet IID multisource block belongs to its jointly typical set with probability tending to one as n tends to infinity.

For an attainable joint n-type q and a fixed v-block of type q_V, its joint-type fiber has cardinality equal to the product of the positive-row conditional type-class cardinalities and at most exp(nH_q(U | V)).
For fixed finite nonempty alphabets U,V, conditional entropy H_q(U | V) is continuous on the joint probability simplex.

For every nonempty S and every supported joint block of a finite IID multisource, the conditional block probability given its complement is the product of the corresponding one-letter conditional probabilities.

published_dependencies.used_for: Finite probability vectors, natural-log entropy, zero-mass conventions, and directional KL divergence.
Mutual independence across source times and the inverse-image argument preserving IID under finite-valued coordinate functions.
The variance tail bound used by the external finite-alphabet information AEP supplier.
Continuity of t ln t at zero through the external relative-entropy continuity lemma, and polynomial-versus-exponential decay in Slepian–Wolf achievability.
Logarithm order and algebra in information units and the binary symmetric example.

seams_checked.note: The finite IID vector source and information-density definitions agree with the prerequisite. The AEP is applied to the finite joint alphabet with its stated support restriction and variance bound.

Conditional type classes use attainable positive-length row types and only the supplied upper cardinality bound. Conditional-entropy continuity applies the relative-entropy continuity supplier with a full-support uniform reference law.

The lossy theorem citations preserve the finite IID and support-restricted typicality interfaces; absolute empirical tolerance is correctly reduced to relative tolerance using the minimum positive source mass. The companion lossless examples state the Slepian–Wolf subset inequalities faithfully.
